ops.title: In-flight cross-repo effort (started 2026-07-02): cc-vigil sleep inhibitor + cc-transcript typed-Rust refactor

ops.body:
cc-vigil is a Swift macOS sleep inhibitor (menu-bar app + user LaunchAgent daemon + root
LaunchDaemon helper + CLI) that keeps the Mac awake while local Claude Code agents are
*truly* working, judged by a transcript oracle, never by Stop/UserPromptSubmit hook
refcounts (adrafinil's issue #7 — NOTE: fixed upstream in adrafinil v1.4.0, closed
2026-07-06, via SubagentStop refcounting + process sniffing; cc-vigil's differentiator is
now the STRUCTURAL fix, not "theirs is unfixed"). Clamshell blocked via root
`pmset -a disablesleep`; display sleep must never be inhibited; battery (20% floor) +
thermal cutouts with hysteresis latches.

Approved plan: `/Users/yasyf/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-10/plans/part-of-cc-runtime-can-enumerated-wilkes.md`.
Backlog: `cc-notes` tasks on the cc-runtime repo. Deliberately NOT in cc-runtime or
cc-orchestrate (standalone tool watching ~/.claude/projects sees every session).

Phases: A1 typed parse-once Rust refactor of cc-transcript (zero-diff gate) → A2 activity
oracle (port of captain-hook `is_waiting`, conditions.py:54-71) + PyO3 → A3 swift-bridge
CCTranscript SPM package (committed XCFramework) → B1 scaffold cc-vigil (repo-bootstrap
skill) → B2 core → B3 sign/notarize via yasyf/homebrew-tap actions → B4 adversarial verify.

**Why:** hooks carry no idle semantics anywhere in this design; the oracle decides, hooks
only nudge latency.
**How to apply:** if resuming, check native TaskList + cc-notes status first; cc-transcript
had moved past the plan's citations once already (9.0.0, new command.rs/protocol.rs) —
re-orient against current code before trusting plan line numbers.

**Status (2026-07-08):** A1–B4 done. **v0.1.1 SHIPPED & independently verified** —
notarized/stapled Developer ID (team SXKCTF23Q2), cask live at `yasyf/tap/cc-vigil`
(sha256 matches asset). All phases complete; only the user's hardware E2E remains.
The E2E playbook now lives in **cc-notes, not a repo md** (user directive: playbooks
belong in cc-notes): runbook = doc `295f932` ("cc-vigil hardware E2E playbook", when-triggered),
checklist = task `1879032` with one criterion per drill; both in the cc-runtime store,
cross-linked. `docs/MANUAL-E2E.md` was deleted (commit 96a81479). Still gates 25797dc.

- **B3 fix (v0.1.0, 02262da):** `SMAuthorizedClients` named the app id, not the daemon's —
  would've refused the privileged daemon→helper XPC in Release. Both the OS gate and runtime
  CallerVerifier now require `dev.yasyf.cc-vigil.daemon` + team OU.
- **B4 cross-cutting sweep found 2 real defects, both fixed in v0.1.1** (cc-notes 2bd007d,
  631a979, done): (1) the human-wait-hint discount in `Oracle.swift` short-circuited before the
  pending-async check → a SILENT `run_in_background`/Monitor job lost its hold ~60s after Stop
  when the idle Notification fired (the exact issue-#7 case, even mis-documented as by-design).
  Fix = gate the discount on `hasMachineDrivenPending` (incl. `.waitingTool` = Monitor/
  ScheduleWakeup/SendMessage/TeamCreate) + HintTracker only sets the hint for genuine
  human-wait `notification_type` kinds (idle_prompt/agent_needs_input/elicitation_dialog/
  *permission_prompt; nil/unknown → fail toward staying awake). (2) `Uninstaller` now does a
  verified `disablesleep` clear before unregistering; helper SIGTERM bounded-retries.
- **Codex/gpt-5.5 lane was UNAVAILABLE the entire session** (every invocation SIGTERM-killed
  before output — environmental, not prompt/repo). Per routing rules, the B3 security review,
  B4 audits, and the v0.1.1 self-review all ran on fable as the sanctioned fallback. A gpt-5.5
  cross-check of the v0.1.1 fixes is a clean follow-up once that lane is healthy.

**Status (2026-07-09, v0.2.0 SHIPPED):** the 50-agent post-ship review (report:
`~/.cc-pool/accounts/acct-08/plans/review-the-implementation-of-rustling-sundae.md`) found
3 HIGH oracle holes past v0.1.1 — H1 permission-hint never clears on approval (no
PreToolUse hook), H2 cross-turn background work invisible (captain-hook d2e07cc drift:
Stop-payload background_tasks/session_crons discarded by the nudge; compaction opens
turns), H3 subagent sidechain files probed with main-session semantics (~41% of finished
agent files pin the block up to 12h) — plus M1 parse-fail-open, M2 recordPush reentrancy,
M3/M4 clear-budget gaps. All fixed across remediation phases 1–4 (46 commits, every one
codex-reviewed, several review rounds each catching real regressions incl. a SIGPIPE
daemon-killer in the PreToolUse nudge path). Shipped as **v0.2.0** (notarized, cask
verified, installed locally via brew upgrade) with the 4 enhancements: release/cutout
notifications, power-transition re-assert, attributed assertion + 900s timeout dead-man
(poll cadences bounded 300s/600s under it), CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR multi-root discovery.
cc-transcript shipped **10.1.0** to PyPI (delivery-aware oracle: has_pending layer,
completion-at-delivery, compact-summary no longer opens turns) — note 10.0.0 had been cut
by another session BEFORE the oracle work merged; the changelog was split to stay honest.
Codex lane came back up mid-day (was down 3 sessions). cc-pool's per-account `projects`
dirs are symlinks into `~/.claude/projects`, so the hardcoded scanner root DOES see pool
sessions today (multi-root support now exists for real relocations). Post-release,
main-CI went green (2 consecutive runs) after converging swiftformat on 0.62.1 (the
macos-26 image pre-installs 0.61.1 and the old `command -v` guard froze CI there — the
lint step now brew-updates, invokes brew's binary explicitly, and echoes its version)
plus a de-flake sweep (guarantee-shaped throttle assertions; generous
eventually-deadlines; timing tests keep lower bounds, drop wall-clock ceilings).

**Follow-up tracks (approved plan, 2026-07-09/10; plan file = the review-the-implementation-of-rustling-sundae.md top section):**
Status 2026-07-10: A SHIPPED (cc-transcript 10.2.0), then the Track-B review caught two
oracle regressions (no Execute→Bash alias lowering; no mcp__ prefix stripping) — fixed
upstream and SHIPPED as **10.4.0** after a version race (another session cut a different
10.3.0; ours re-cut as 10.4.0 via isolated-worktree rebase). **Pin/lock target =
e04b44c** (10.4.0 release tip; tag v10.4.0 → ec12a33); docs tip 0f04e6a. The oracle is
now alias-/MCP-aware in BOTH backends incl. the human-facing mid-tool check (matters:
cc-runtime serves AskUserQuestion over MCP). Track B: is_waiting → probe_events rewrite
9c3b6ec + 10.4.0 convergence 5f2a369 (two un-flips + sentinel/spy layering test), 2335
green — captain-hook 8.16.0 release in flight. Track C SHIPPED to cc-vigil main
(e8bd39f/33a137e/341afcd, CI green): SessionPidTracker, .sessionProcessDead pre-cliff
discount, live-past-cliff (bounded by process lifetime — accepted design), two-seam
discovery pinning + dead-entry pruning. Track D SHIPPED to main (9330c65/1372f0d/b91a5b4,
CI green): daemon-composed SleepAlert ring + persisted monotonic ids + optional
StatusReport.alerts + exact-once app watermark (only-forward, post-then-advance,
persisted alertedCutouts); accepted residuals: OS-delivery best-effort, ring ageout,
daemon-crash windows — events.log/away summary = ground truth. Track E in flight (Low
Power cutout + tolerant CutoutKind decoding, App Intents, sfltool hint, pin bump to
e04b44c); THEN orchestrator-authored README/CHANGELOG docs pass, ship v0.3.0. Process
notes: fetch-before-push + auto-bump-minor-on-version-race are standing release
procedure; review lanes = codex wrapper with a SECOND fresh wrapper before any Claude
fallback (guard-enforced); delegated prose must READ the writing-docs skill or be
orchestrator-authored.

**Remaining after v0.2.0:** (1) the user's hardware E2E (25797dc; checklist gained 3
items: clamshell power-transition, logout dead-man drill, cowork-host argv observation);
(2) per-session liveness 0b9f2b5 (still open; nudges now carry claudePid + roots, making
it easier); (3) captain-hook convergence follow-up — the Rust oracle deliberately LEADS
the reference on compact-summary turn handling; (4) SleepNotifier disconnect-gap
limitations are documented-by-design (events.log/away summary are ground truth).
